# Bounded review — M2-01 native mutation writer (read-only, no tools run)

I reviewed only the files supplied in the prompt. I did not compile, run tests, or inspect `host_config.rs`, `stdio/mutation.rs`, `application/mutation.rs`, `source.rs`, or `SOURCE_MAX_FILE_BYTES`. Nothing below asserts qualification; findings are derived from the code as written. Scope respected: only the writer, journal, recovery, metadata, quota, authorization surface of the root-lint cut.

---

## P0

**1. `receipt()` and `recover()` fail closed on store quota and on any unknown store entry — the two operations that must work when the store is unhealthy.**
`filesystem/macos/mutation.rs::receipt` and `::recover` both call `self.check_quota()?` before loading the journal. `check_quota` returns `LimitExceeded` when `bytes > MAX_STORE_BYTES` and `RecoveryRequired` for any entry it does not recognise. Consequences, both reachable:

- 256 MiB is reachable with ~6 journals at the 48 MiB entry cap. Once crossed, a workspace left at `Published` (source swapped, `.rust-mcp-mut-*.swap` still present) has **no MCP path to completion**: `recover` returns `LimitExceeded`, retention/cleanup CLI is not implemented, and ADR-052 tells the operator not to delete the directory.
- A single stray file in the state dir (`.DS_Store`, an editor artifact, an interrupted `write_new`) makes every `receipt` and `recover` return `RecoveryRequired` for *all* ids, so even reading evidence for an unrelated completed mutation is blocked.

This contradicts ADR-052's "no se elimina evidencia para conseguir espacio" combined with "recuperación conservadora" — conservative recovery has to remain *reachable*.

**Fix:** remove `check_quota()` from `receipt` and `recover`. Keep quota enforcement only on the write path (`ensure_quota_for` in `commit_checked`, and the pre-write check in `persist`). Split the store-consistency scan out of `check_quota` and apply it only to `commit_checked`; `receipt`/`recover` should resolve one journal by exact name and report on it. `persist` inside `recover_locked` must be allowed to exceed the byte quota by the size of one record (recovery completion is not new work).

---

## P1

**2. `make_receipt` reports planned bytes as observed state for non-`Committed` receipts.**
`make_receipt(body)` always builds `files[0].before/after` from `body.before`/`body.after`, regardless of `state`. So a `RecoveryRequired` receipt after an external overwrite (exactly your `post_swap_interrupt_and_late_external_write_are_classified` case, where disk holds `b"external bytes"`) reports `after: sha256(<planned lints manifest>)` — a hash that never existed on disk — and a `NoChange` receipt after a rollback reports the *changed* hash. ADR-050 §7 requires the receipt to declare before/after and the changes actually made.
**Fix:** thread the observed `(bytes, node)` already computed in `recover_locked`/`receipt` into `make_receipt`, and for any state other than `Committed` report `after` as the observed on-disk fingerprint, plus an explicit `intended` field if the plan hash is still wanted.

**3. Replay of an aborted plan returns `MutationState::NoChange`, conflating two different outcomes.**
`commit_checked` → `load()` returns a `Staged` body → `recover_locked` takes the `active == before_bytes && temp == after_bytes` branch → `AbortedCleanup` → `NoChange`. The peer asked for a changing patch and receives `NoChange`, indistinguishable from "your candidate was byte-identical". A client that treats `NoChange` as success will report the lint change as applied.
**Fix:** add a distinct terminal state (e.g. `Aborted`) in `domain/src/mutation.rs::MutationState`, or have the replay path return `MutationError::Conflict` with the journal left terminal so the peer must re-preview. `validate_candidate` already knows `changed`; use it to detect the mismatch.

**4. Swap failure discards the real cause and over-reports recovery.**
```rust
if self.swap(lease, &body.temp_path).is_err() {
    let _ = self.recover_locked(lease, body);
    return Err(MutationError::RecoveryRequired);
}
```
`swap` can fail with `EWOULDBLOCK`/`EPERM`/`ENOENT` having produced no effect; `recover_locked` then proves no effect and rolls the temp back, yet the caller still sees `RecoveryRequired`, which per your own docs instructs the developer to stop and preserve evidence. This is inconsistent with `abort_before_effect`, which correctly returns `original` on a clean `NoChange`.
**Fix:** `let error = mutation_io(err); return Err(self.abort_before_effect(lease, body, error));`

**5. No manifest size bound on the `after` side in `validate_candidate`.**
`read_workspace_file_with_node` bounds by `SOURCE_MAX_FILE_BYTES`, but M1 manifest reads (`macos.rs::Access::read_file`) reject above `MAX_FILE_BYTES = 256 KiB`, and ADR-052 states the 256 KiB editor limit applies before the general limit. Nothing in `validate_candidate` / `validate_manifest_patch` enforces it, so a successful commit can publish a `Cargo.toml` that `SecureProjects::open` subsequently rejects with `OutputLimitExceeded` — a committed change that bricks the project for every M1 tool.
**Fix:** in `validate_candidate`, reject when `after_cargo.bytes().len() > 256 * 1024` (`MutationError::LimitExceeded`).

**6. State-root/project overlap is checked only against write roots.**
`NativeMutationStore::open` rejects overlap between `checked_state` and `write_roots`, but the store never sees the read `--root`s. If `--state-root` sits under a read root, M1 source capture will pull `rust-mcp-mutations-v1/journal-*.json` into peer-visible output — journal bodies carry full before/after manifest bytes, idempotency keys and operation ids. ADR-052 explicitly rejected "journal en el proyecto".
**Fix:** pass the full read-root set into `NativeMutationStore::open` and apply the same bidirectional `starts_with` rejection, or assert it in host config at startup and fail before serving.

**7. Per-commit journal scanning cost is superlinear and unmeasured.**
`check_quota`, `reject_reused_key` and `reject_workspace_pending` each independently `Dir::read_from` the store and, for every journal, `read_optional` (full read) + `decode` (JSON parse + SHA-256 over a re-serialised body + full `mutation_digest` over both bundles). `persist` calls `check_quota` again on every phase transition (≥4 per commit), and `recover_locked` persists up to three times. At the documented ceiling (128 journals, 48 MiB entries) that is hundreds of MiB of reads and hashes per commit. ADR-050 lists commit duration as a closure blocker.
**Fix:** perform one directory scan per commit and share the decoded index across the three predicates; skip `mutation_digest` re-verification for entries not being acted on (checksum alone suffices for the quota/key/pending scan), and drop `check_quota` from `persist` in favour of the reservation already taken by `ensure_quota_for`.

---

## P2

8. `macos.rs::flags` sets `UNIQUE = 0x0000_2000`, which — unlike `NOFOLLOW_ANY` and `RESOLVE_BENEATH` — has **no startup probe** in `SecureProjects::new`. Either add a discriminating probe or drop the flag; an unprobed magic bit in the open path of every write is not evidence-backed.
9. `create_temp` compares `st_mode`/`st_uid`/`st_gid`/`st_flags`/xattrs between source and clone but never compares ACLs, even though `CLONE_SAFE_METADATA` includes the ACL bit. Add an `acl_get_fd` comparison or state in the receipt that ACL preservation is kernel-supplied and unverified.
10. `JournalPhase::rank()` collapses all five terminal-ish phases to `2`, so `load`'s `(Some, Some)` arm cannot order two same-rank records. Add a monotonically increasing `sequence: u64` to `JournalBody`, include it in `same_binding` as a strict `staging.sequence > final.sequence` requirement.
11. `receipt()` calls `load()`, which renames a staging record over the final one and `durable()`s. `receipt` is documented as the non-repairing query. Split a read-only resolution path that reports the ambiguity instead of resolving it.
12. `workspace-{dev}-{ino}.lock` files are created on demand, never removed, and are `continue`d past in `check_quota` before byte accounting — unbounded, unaccounted directory growth as workspace inodes churn.
13. `mutation_store.rs::mutation_digest` hardcodes `field(&mut hash, b"manifest_patch")` instead of deriving the tag from `candidate.kind`; a second `MutationKind` variant will silently share the digest domain.
14. A leftover `.journal-*.json.staging` wedges `persist` permanently (`replace` → `read_optional(staging).is_some()` → `RecoveryRequired`) on paths that reach `persist` without a prior `load` — notably `abort_before_effect` → `recover_locked` → `persist`. Have `replace` resolve an own, checksum-valid, same-binding staging record rather than refusing.
15. `second_store_observes_global_lock_as_busy` exercises two stores in one process. `flock` is per open-file-description so it does demonstrate fd-level exclusion, but ADR-052 claims coordination *between processes*; a spawned-process test is needed before that claim is qualified.
16. `validate_lints_delta` permits removal and downgrade (`unsafe_code = "forbid"` → `"allow"`, or deletion via the `else { continue }` branch). That is inside the delegated scope, but the receipt currently surfaces only hashes; add an explicit per-lint delta summary so a downgrade is visible without diffing.
17. `mutation_state.rs::prepare_mutation_state` does not run `checked_path(parent)` (unlike `StateRoot::open`); `//`, `.`/`..` and control characters are only caught later. Apply it up front for a single validation contract.

---

## Verdict

**Revise.**

The authorization spine (exact-root grant, lease dev/ino retention, `authorize_body` binding, deny-by-default) and the inode-plus-bytes classification in `recover_locked` are sound as written, and the pre-effect abort paths look correct against the checkpoints shown. But P0/1 makes conservative recovery unreachable exactly when it is needed, and P1/2 and P1/3 mean the receipt — the artifact the whole contract rests on — can state an effect that did not occur. Those two must land before this cut can be presented as a qualified writer. P1/5 and P1/6 are small, mechanical, and close real contract gaps against ADR-052. I would not treat any part of M2 as Done on this cut, consistent with the outstanding gate, retention CLI, notices and docs.
